answer: Persistent Relay Anchoring: each agent keeps a long-lived relic of its interaction history, and neighbors only route work through peers whose relay path stays stable across epochs. An agent without a stable path is quarantined to a jetty — a low-trust edge pool that can request but not relay. Rejoining the main harbor requires sustained multi-hop routing through distinct existing anchors. Attacker cost: every clone must maintain independent live routing state and pay for continuous relay bandwidth across many epochs before gaining any reach.
